description: Data from a study of the climatic suitability of eight key crops in Bhutan under current climate and a high-emission scenario (RCP 8.5) for 2050. The Dataverse record says it was a joint initiative of Bhutan's Ministry of Agriculture and Forests, CIAT and UNEP, funded through the Asia-Pacific Climate Technology Network and Finance Center, with two aims: building national capacity to produce suitability maps and assess uncertainties, and assessing climate change impacts on growing areas for crops including maize, rice, potato, chilli and tomato. The 14 files include a readme, biophysical data, geodata on current and 2050 climate, climate change, elevation, slope, soil, solar radiation and soil erosion, and crop suitability for current, future and change periods plus maps, as zip archives up to about 157 MB. It was first released on 24 August 2017 and last updated on 8 July 2019 by CIAT, free to download under custom terms. Caveats: one emission scenario and one future period are covered. For simulation it gives national crop suitability shifts for a mountain country, to plan adaptation of farming and irrigation. Related catalogue records include FAO-IIASA GAEZ and the LS-500 global cropland suitability maps.
